title: Peter Thiel says Obama and Pope Leo are exploiting AI fears in his latest Antichrist lectures
key_facts: Thiel spoke in closed-door lectures in Nashville on 28 Sep and 5 Oct, per recordings obtained by Politico's Decoded
He said many people know AI is politically unpopular and use that to boost their own popularity, naming Obama and the pope
He suggested the pope found AI to distract from the Church's abuse scandals
He said effective altruism has 'brainwashed' many people working on AI
He frames efforts to regulate AI as a path to one-world government (the Antichrist lecture series)
Obama recently urged Democrats to develop an AI plan; Pope Leo's encyclical Magnifica Humanitas was released in May
Thiel's representatives did not respond to Politico
quote_evidence: "Many people know that AI is politically unpopular and want to leverage that to boost their own popularity," Thiel said. "Both Obama and the pope fall into this category."
Thiel's representatives did not respond to Politico's request for comment.
why_it_matters_hint: The AI-regulation debate now draws in religion and electoral politics.
notes: inkl page blocked (403); read Fortune's report, which credits Politico's Decoded for the recordings.
